reading: Each entry records what was read. The first investigation (Codex, 8 October) read sections of the first six; research agents re-read those the same day and found the rest through web search and fetch, PDF viewing and publisher or repository full text. Where an agent quoted a source without itemising its reading, the entry says so. Titles appear only where a reader saw them. Nothing here is admitted as a manuscript source, and no outside bytes are kept.

sources.citation: G. A. Landis, Thermoradiative Arrays: A New Technology for Conversion of Heat into Electrical Power. Nuclear and Emerging Technologies for Space (NETS-2022), Cleveland, 8-12 May 2022
sources.kind: proposal, with ideal efficiencies quoted from others
used_for: a thermoradiative converter serves both as the energy converter and as the waste-heat radiator
proposed on the shaded side of a solar array as a bottoming cycle, and as the radiator of a Stirling or Brayton converter; suggestions without analysis
the array's front would then need low infrared emissivity, since silica cover glass emits in the infrared; photovoltaics work best cold, so the array runs warmer
thermoradiative converters radiate less than blackbodies, so the radiator may be larger; at high temperature they may suit a small radiator

ideal efficiencies quoted: Strandberg, up to 68% between 1000 K and 300 K at fractions of a milliwatt per square metre and about 22% near peak power; Fernandez, 20-22.5%; thermoelectrics about 6% in space
on an airless body by day the radiator has to be shielded from the Sun, Earth and the hot surface

sources.citation: V. Radchenkov, J. A. Harrison, M. H. Sazzad, P. M. Pearce, A. Pusch, S. P. Bremner, P. J. Reece, N. J. Ekins-Daukes, M. P. Nielsen, Temperature-dependent power generation from HgCdTe and III-V thermoradiative diodes. Appl. Phys. Lett. 126, 173901 (2025)
sources.read: authors' manuscript, main text (UNSWorks); the publisher's page was unavailable; supplement unread
used_for: best stated measurement 9.41 mW/m^2: an MCT-5 HgCdTe diode at 292.5 K facing a 150 K cold emissive surface, in vacuum
commercial photodetectors with 0.1 x 0.1 mm active area on GaAs immersion lenses; the other devices give 1-6 mW/m^2
device models overestimate the current and match one device; HgCdTe devices are safe to 330 K, III-V devices beyond 400 K
a thermoradiative diode needs no intermediate cold surface, unlike engines that work through radiative cooling

sources.citation: S. Buddhiraju, P. Santhanam, S. Fan, Thermodynamic limits of energy harvesting from outgoing thermal radiation. PNAS 115, E3609-E3615 (2018)
sources.read: full text (arXiv 1710.02617 v1) and publication metadata
used_for: for a 300 K body facing 3 K space, ideal harvested power: 54.8 W/m^2 single junction, 48.4 W/m^2 through a blackbody intermediate at 225.1 K, 55.0 W/m^2 multicolour, 153.1 W/m^2 the Landsberg limit, which needs nonreciprocal elements
ideal conditions: blackbodies, full-hemisphere exchange, a 3 K sink

sources.citation: D. Melanson, M. Abu Khater, M. Aifer, K. Donatella, M. Hunter Gordon, T. Ahle, G. Crooks, A. J. Martinez, F. Sbahi, P. J. Coles, Thermodynamic computing system for AI applications. Nat. Commun. 16, 3757 (2025)
sources.kind: eight-cell prototype measured; larger advantages modelled
sources.read: full text (PMC12015238, targeted extraction) and sections of the published PDF
used_for: eight RLC cells on a circuit board, all-to-all coupled through switched capacitors; noise from a digitally generated random bit stream; FPGA control; 10-bit readout
Gaussian sampling and the inversion of an 8 x 8 matrix on three copies of the board, about 12,000 samples, with relative errors of 25-31% (preprint)
modelled against a measured GPU: crossover near dimension 3,000, an order of magnitude in time and energy at 10,000, with 0.005 mW per cell dominated by the analogue-to-digital converters
in a simulated chip design the converters draw 40-200 uW against 0.2-3 uW for the computing core

sources.citation: M. Aifer et al., Thermodynamic linear algebra. npj Unconv. Comput. 1, 13 (2024)
sources.read: quoted by a research agent; reading not itemised
used_for: matrix inversion, linear systems and the Lyapunov equation by sampling, with speedups growing linearly in dimension and runtime growing as the inverse square of the error tolerance

sources.citation: S. Whitelam, C. Casert, Nonlinear thermodynamic computing out of equilibrium. Nat. Commun. 17, 1189 (2026)
sources.read: full text (PMC12858898, targeted extraction; arXiv 2412.17183 v3)
used_for: a simulated thermodynamic neural network needs a single thermal bath and gives its output at a prescribed observation time: run, observe, reset, about a thousand times
no hardware; the energy of resetting and reading is left uncounted

sources.citation: C. Kathmann, M. Reina, R. Messina, P. Ben-Abdallah, S.-A. Biehs, Scalable radiative thermal logic gates based on nanoparticle networks. Sci. Rep. 10, 3596 (2020)
sources.read: full text (arXiv v1) and the publisher's main text
used_for: logic gates from the near-field heat exchange of VO2 nanoparticles near their 340 K transition, computed in steady state
gates do not connect simply, since radiative exchange is not additive; the authors find the speed suited to thermal management and sensing and uncompetitive with electronics for computing
